results.message: With 90 minutes in T3 you've got time for a proper coffee. Bacha Coffee is the standout: a stunning Moroccan-style space with 200+ Arabica options, but it's takeaway only, so grab a cup and sip it near your gate. If you'd rather sit down, Starbucks has the best seating in the terminal with counter seats facing the atrium glass, and The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf is usually quieter with good terminal views. It's peak dinner time, so queues could add 10-20 minutes depending on the venue.

results.message: For a proper nap, the Snooze Lounge in T1 is your best bet: it's free, open 24/7, and has reclining chairs with dimmed lighting, a quiet zone, and little privacy screens. It's first-come-first-served, and it tends to be at its best late at night, so at 7:19 pm it may be busier or less hushed than it will be later. If you'd like a real bed and a shower, the Ambassador Transit Hotel and Crowne Plaza Changi Airport both offer day-use rooms, which makes sense with your 240 minutes. Availability can vary, so check at the front desk.

results.message: For proper local flavours in T2, I'd start with Heavenly Wang, a kopitiam-style spot where you can get real Singapore kopi, teh and kaya toast, plus a solid nasi lemak set that's very easy on the wallet. The T2 Food Gallery is also great for variety, with hawker-style stalls serving Hainanese chicken rice, laksa and nasi lemak under one roof, and it's open 24/7. If you just want a quick snack, Old Chang Kee's curry puff is the classic local grab-and-go (it closes at 9 pm, so you've got a little time tonight).

results.message: Six hours at T3 is a great window, so you can have a proper dinner, a little rest, and still see the sights. Since it's peak dinner time, Din Tai Fung will likely have a queue (budget 45-60 min including the wait), but the xiaolongbao and steamed chicken soup are worth it. Afterwards, the rooftop Sunflower Garden is lovely around dusk and evening lighting, and with this much time you could book a pod at YOTELAIR for a proper sleep, no immigration needed.

results.message: Great news: T4 is a handy spot for souvenirs, and you've got plenty of time. Start at Taste Singapore for edible gifts like laksa paste, chilli crab sauce and kaya jam, then pop into Zakkasg for budget-friendly Japanese stationery and small gifts. Lego Airport Store is a must if anyone at home collects, since it has Changi-themed sets you can't get elsewhere, and the Build a Minifigure station is fun (allow about 20 minutes). If you'd like a little extra, the Heritage Zone is a free, interactive Peranakan exhibit, and Lotte Duty Free is good for liquor and cosmetics before boarding.

results.message: With about 5 hours in T1, you've got plenty of time to freshen up properly. The Ambassador Transit Hotel is a great pick: non-guest access includes shower and towels, plus a rooftop pool with runway views and a jacuzzi, which makes a lovely pre-flight reset. If you want a more private option, Crowne Plaza Changi Airport is connected directly to T1 and offers day-use rooms with shower facilities. If you hold Priority Pass, the SATS Premier Lounge is also a decent quiet spot to freshen up, though I'd confirm shower availability when you arrive. Access terms and availability can vary, so check at the desk.

results.message:
Since it's peak dinner time, expect queues, but you have plenty of room. Here's an easy walking route:

1. Sunflower Garden (~10 min): a calm rooftop with a runway view to unwind after your last flight.
2. T2 Food Gallery (~20 min, maybe longer at peak): the flagship hawker hall. Go for the laksa or chicken rice stalls, since the queues there are worth it.
3. Orchid Garden & Koi Pond (~10 min): 700+ orchids and a quiet koi pond for a relaxed walk after eating.
4. Kenangan Coffee (~10 min): try the es kopi susu.
5. dnata Lounge (~20 min): pay-per-use, with a shower and a genuinely good nasi lemak if you want to rest before boarding.

If you'd rather sit down, Din Tai Fung (xiaolongbao, plus the steamed chicken soup) and Peach Garden (Chinese dim sum) are both open now. Din Tai Fung closes at 9pm, so eat there before then. This route uses about 70 of your 135 usable minutes, which leaves a comfortable 15-minute gate buffer even if the queues run long.

results.message: You've got a comfortable window before your 21:50 boarding for SQ322, so here's a relaxed T3 route. 1) Start with the Butterfly Garden (about 20 min): 1,000 butterflies across 40 species and a 6-metre waterfall make it a calming reset before a long-haul to London. 2) Then have dinner. It's peak dinner time, so expect waits of roughly 20-45 min at sit-down spots. Sushi Tei is worth booking ahead on the Changi Food app (the baked cheese roll and salmon belly sashimi get great reviews), or O'Coffee Club is a good sit-down option with generous portions. 3) If time's left, stretch your legs with a short stop at the Koi Pond or Sunflower Garden, whose evening lighting is lovely, then head to your gate with the 15-minute buffer in hand. T3 is spacious, so allow a good walk back. Boarding is at 21:50, so aim to be heading to the gate by about 21:35.
